sections.label: SEC. 7001.
sections.heading: DEFINITIONS
sections.title: VII
sections.own_text: In this title, the following definitions apply:

children.heading: Coastal louisiana ecosystem
children.own_text: The term ``coastal Louisiana ecosystem'' means the coastal area of Louisiana from the Sabine River on the west to the Pearl River on the east, including those parts of the Atchafalaya River Basin and the Mississippi River Deltaic Plain below the Old River Control Structure and the Chenier Plain included within the study area of the restoration plan.

children.heading: Governor
children.own_text: The term ``Governor'' means the Governor of the State of Louisiana.

children.heading: Restoration plan
children.own_text: The term ``restoration plan'' means the report of the Chief of Engineers for ecosystem restoration for the Louisiana Coastal Area dated January 31, 2005.

children.heading: Task force
children.own_text: The term ``Task Force'' means the Coastal Louisiana Ecosystem Protection and Restoration Task Force established by section 7003.

children.heading: Comprehensive plan
children.own_text: The term ``comprehensive plan'' means the plan developed under section 7002 and any revisions thereto.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: The Secretary, in coordination with the Governor, shall develop a comprehensive plan for protecting, preserving, and restoring the coastal Louisiana ecosystem.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Integration of Plan Into Comprehensive Hurricane Protection Study
children.own_text: In developing the comprehensive plan, the Secretary shall integrate the restoration plan into the analysis and design of the comprehensive hurricane protection study authorized by title I of the Energy and Water Development Appropriations Act, 2006 (119 Stat. 2247).

children.label: (c)
children.heading: Consistency With Comprehensive Coastal Protection Master Plan
children.own_text: In developing the comprehensive plan, the Secretary shall ensure that the plan is not inconsistent with the goals, analysis, and design of the comprehensive coastal protection master plan authorized and defined pursuant to Act 8 of the First Extraordinary Session of the Louisiana State Legislature, 2005.

children.label: (d)
children.heading: Inclusions
children.own_text: The comprehensive plan shall include a description of--

the framework of a long-term program integrated with hurricane and storm damage reduction, flood damage reduction, and navigation activities that provide for the comprehensive protection, conservation, and restoration of the wetlands, estuaries, barrier islands, shorelines, and related land and features of the coastal Louisiana ecosystem, including protection of critical resources, habitat, and infrastructure from the effects of a coastal storm, a hurricane, erosion, or subsidence;
the means by which a new technology, or an improved technique, can be integrated into the program referred to in paragraph (1);
the role of other Federal and State agencies and programs in carrying out such program;
specific, measurable success criteria (including ecological criteria) by which success of the plan will be measured;
proposed projects in order of priority as determined by their respective potential to contribute to--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: creation of coastal wetlands; and

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: flood protection of communities ranked by population density and level of protection; and
efforts by Federal, State, and local interests to address sociological, economic, and related fields of law.

children.label: (e)
children.heading: Considerations
children.own_text: In developing the comprehensive plan, the Secretary shall consider the advisability of integrating into the program referred to in subsection (d)(1)--

an investigation and study of the maximum effective use of the water and sediment of the Mississippi and Atchafalaya Rivers for coastal restoration purposes consistent with flood control and navigation;
a schedule for the design and implementation of large- scale water and sediment reintroduction projects and an assessment of funding needs from any source;
an investigation and assessment of alterations in the operation of the Old River Control Structure, consistent with flood control and navigation purposes;
any related Federal or State project being carried out on the date on which the plan is developed;
any activity in the restoration plan; and
any other project or activity identified in one or more of--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: the Mississippi River and Tributaries program;

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: the Louisiana Coastal Wetlands Conservation Plan;

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: the Louisiana Coastal Zone Management Plan;

children.label: (D)
children.own_text: the plan of the State of Louisiana entitled ``Integrated Ecosystem Restoration and Hurricane Protection--Louisiana's Comprehensive Master Plan for a Sustainable Coast''; and

children.label: (E)
children.own_text: other relevant reports as determined by the Secretary.

children.heading: Initial report
children.own_text: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report containing the comprehensive plan.

children.heading: Updates
children.own_text: Not later than 5 years after the date of submission of a report under paragraph (1), and at least once every 5 years thereafter until implementation of the comprehensive plan is complete, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report containing an update of the plan and an assessment of the progress made in implementing the plan.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: The Secretary may carry out a program for ecosystem restoration, Louisiana Coastal Area, Louisiana, substantially in accordance with the report of the Chief of Engineers, dated January 31, 2005.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: In carrying out the program under subsection (a), the Secretary shall give priority to--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: any portion of the program identified in the report described in subsection (a) as a critical restoration feature;

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: any Mississippi River diversion project that--

children.label: (i)
children.own_text: will protect a major population area of the Pontchartrain, Pearl, Breton Sound, Barataria, or Terrebonne basins; and

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: will produce an environmental benefit to the coastal Louisiana ecosystem;

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: any barrier island, or barrier shoreline, project that--

children.label: (i)
children.own_text: will be carried out in conjunction with a Mississippi River diversion project; and

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: will protect a major population area;

children.label: (D)
children.own_text: any project that will reduce storm surge and prevent or reduce the risk of loss of human life and the risk to public safety; and

children.label: (E)
children.own_text: a project to physically modify the Mississippi River-Gulf Outlet and to restore the areas affected by the Mississippi River-Gulf Outlet in accordance with the comprehensive plan to be developed under section 7002(a) and consistent with sections 7006(c)(1)(A) and 7013.

sections.label: SEC. 7004.
sections.heading: COASTAL LOUISIANA ECOSYSTEM PROTECTION AND RESTORATION TASK FORCE
sections.title: VII

children.label: (a)
children.heading: Establishment
children.own_text: There is established a task force to be known as the Coastal Louisiana Ecosystem Protection and Restoration Task Force (in this section referred to as the ``Task Force'').

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Membership
children.own_text: The Task Force shall consist of the following members (or, in the case of the head of a Federal agency, a designee of the head of the agency at the level of Assistant Secretary or an equivalent level):
The Secretary.
The Secretary of the Interior.
The Secretary of Commerce.
The Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency.
The Secretary of Agriculture.
The Secretary of Transportation.
The Secretary of Energy.
The Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency.
The Commandant of the Coast Guard.
The Chair of the Coastal Protection and Restoration Authority of Louisiana.
Two representatives of the State of Louisiana selected by the Governor.

children.label: (c)
children.heading: Duties
children.own_text: The Task Force shall make recommendations to the Secretary regarding--
policies, strategies, plans, programs, projects, and activities for addressing conservation, protection, restoration, and maintenance of the coastal Louisiana ecosystem;
financial participation by each agency represented on the Task Force in conserving, protecting, restoring, and maintaining the coastal Louisiana ecosystem, including recommendations--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: that identify funds from current agency missions and budgets; and

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: for coordinating individual agency budget requests; and
the comprehensive plan to be developed under section 7002(a).

children.label: (d)
children.heading: Report
children.own_text: The Task Force shall submit to Congress a biennial report that summarizes the activities and recommendations of the Task Force.

children.heading: General authority
children.own_text: The Task Force may establish such working groups as the Task Force determines to be necessary to assist the Task Force in carrying out this section.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: Integration team
children.own_text: The Task Force shall establish a working group for the purpose of advising the Task Force of opportunities to integrate the planning, engineering, design, implementation, and performance of Corps of Engineers projects for hurricane and storm damage reduction, flood damage reduction, ecosystem restoration, and navigation in those areas in Louisiana for which a major disaster has been declared by the President as a result of Hurricane Katrina or Rita.

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Expertise; representation
children.own_text: In establishing the working group under subparagraph (A), the Task Force shall ensure that the group--

children.label: (i)
children.own_text: has expertise in coastal estuaries, diversions, coastal restoration and wetlands protection, ecosystem restoration, hurricane protection, storm damage reduction systems, navigation, and ports; and

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: represents the State of Louisiana and local governments in southern Louisiana.

children.label: (C)
children.heading: Duties
children.own_text: In developing its recommendations under this subsection, the working group shall--

children.label: (i)
children.own_text: review reports relating to the performance of, and recommendations relating to the future performance of, the hurricane, coastal, and flood protection systems in southern Louisiana, including the reports issued by the Interagency Performance Evaluation Team, the National Academy of Sciences, the National Science Foundation, the American Society of Civil Engineers, and Team Louisiana for the purpose of advising the Task Force and the Secretary on opportunities to improve the performance of the protection systems;

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: assist in providing reviews under section 2035; and

children.label: (iii)
children.own_text: carry out such other duties as the Task Force or the Secretary determines to be appropriate.

children.label: (f)
children.heading: Compensation
children.own_text: Members of the Task Force and members of a working group established by the Task Force may not receive compensation for their services as members of the Task Force or working group, as the case may be.

children.label: (g)
children.heading: Travel Expenses
children.own_text: Travel expenses incurred by members of the Task Force and members of a working group established by the Task Force, in the performance of their service on the Task Force or working group, as the case may be, shall be paid by the agency or entity that the member represents.

children.label: (h)
children.heading: Nonapplicability of FACA
children.own_text: The Federal Advisory Committee Act (5 U.S.C. App.) shall not apply to the Task Force or any working group established by the Task Force.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: Review
children.own_text: The Secretary, in cooperation with the non-Federal interest of the project involved, shall review each Federally-authorized water resources project in the coastal Louisiana ecosystem being carried out or completed as of the date of enactment of this Act to determine whether the project needs to be modified--
to take into account the program authorized by section 7003 and the projects authorized by sections 7006(e) and 7013; or
to contribute to ecosystem restoration under section 7003, 7006(e), or 7013.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Modifications
children.own_text: Subject to subsections (c) and (d), the Secretary may carry out the modifications described in subsection (a).

children.label: (c)
children.heading: Public Notice and Comment
children.own_text: Before completing the report required under subsection (d), the Secretary shall provide an opportunity for public notice and comment.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: Before modifying an operation or feature of a project under subsection (b), the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate a report describing the modification.

children.heading: Inclusion
children.own_text: A report describing a modification under paragraph (1) shall include such information relating to the timeline for and cost of the modification, as the Secretary determines to be relevant.

children.label: (e)
children.heading: Authorization of Appropriations
children.own_text: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $10,000,000.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The Secretary shall carry out a coastal Louisiana ecosystem science and technology program substantially in accordance with the restoration plan at a total cost of $100,000,000.

children.heading: Purposes
children.own_text: The purposes of the program shall be--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: to identify any uncertainty relating to the physical, chemical, geological, biological, and cultural baseline conditions in the coastal Louisiana ecosystem;

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: to improve knowledge of the physical, chemical, geological, biological, and cultural baseline conditions in the coastal Louisiana ecosystem;

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: to identify and develop technologies, models, and methods to carry out this subsection; and

children.label: (D)
children.own_text: to advance and expedite the implementation of the comprehensive plan.

children.heading: Working groups
children.own_text: The Secretary may establish such working groups as the Secretary determines to be necessary to assist the Secretary in carrying out this subsection.

children.heading: Contracts and cooperative agreements
children.own_text: In carrying out this subsection, the Secretary may enter into a contract or cooperative agreement with a consortium of academic institutions in Louisiana with scientific or engineering expertise in the restoration of aquatic and marine ecosystems for coastal restoration and enhancement through science and technology.

children.heading: Applicability of the federal advisory committee act
children.own_text: The Federal Advisory Committee Act (5 U.S.C. App.) shall not apply to a working group established under this subsection.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: Subject to paragraph (2), the Secretary may carry out demonstration projects substantially in accordance with the restoration plan and within the coastal Louisiana ecosystem for the purpose of resolving critical areas of scientific or technological uncertainty related to the implementation of the comprehensive plan.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: Total cost
children.own_text: The total cost for planning, design, and construction of all projects under this subsection shall not exceed $100,000,000.

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Individual project
children.own_text: The total cost of any single project under this subsection shall not exceed $25,000,000.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The Secretary is authorized to carry out the following projects substantially in accordance with the restoration plan:

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: Mississippi River-Gulf Outlet environmental restoration at a total cost of $105,300,000, but not including those elements of the project that produce navigation benefits.

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: Small diversion at Hope Canal at a total cost of $68,600,000.

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: Barataria basin barrier shoreline restoration at a total cost of $242,600,000.

children.label: (D)
children.own_text: Small Bayou Lafourche reintroduction at a total cost of $133,500,000.

children.label: (E)
children.own_text: Medium diversion at Myrtle Grove with dedicated dredging at a total cost of $278,300,000.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: In general
children.own_text: In carrying out each project under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall carry out such modifications as may be necessary to the ecosystem restoration features identified in the restoration plan--

children.label: (i)
children.own_text: to address the impacts of Hurricanes Katrina and Rita on the areas of the project; and

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: to ensure consistency with the project authorized by section 7013 (including work in and around the vicinity of the Mississippi River-Gulf Outlet).

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Integration
children.own_text: The Secretary shall ensure that each modification under subparagraph (A) is taken into account in conducting the study of comprehensive hurricane protection authorized by title I of the Energy and Water Development Appropriations Act, 2006 (119 Stat. 2247).

children.label: (C)
children.heading: Mississippi river-gulf outlet
children.own_text: In carrying out the project under paragraph (1)(A), the Secretary shall carry out such modifications as may be necessary to make the project consistent with and complementary to the closure and restoration of the Mississippi River-Gulf Outlet authorized by section 7013.

children.heading: Construction reports
children.own_text: Before the Secretary may begin construction of any project under this subsection, the Secretary shall submit a report documenting any modifications to the project, including cost changes, to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate.

children.heading: Applicability of other provisions
children.own_text: Notwithstanding section 902 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1986 (33 U.S.C. 2280), the cost of a project under this subsection, including any modifications to the project, shall not exceed 150 percent of the cost of such project set forth in paragraph (1).

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The Secretary, substantially in accordance with the restoration plan, shall implement in the coastal Louisiana ecosystem a program for the beneficial use of material dredged from federally maintained waterways at a total cost of $100,000,000.

children.heading: Consideration
children.own_text: In carrying out the program under paragraph (1), the Secretary shall consider the beneficial use of sediment from the Illinois River System for wetlands restoration in wetlands-depleted watersheds of the coastal Louisiana ecosystem.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The Secretary is authorized to carry out the following projects referred to in the restoration plan if the Secretary determines such projects are feasible:

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: Land Bridge between Caillou Lake and the Gulf of Mexico at a total cost of $56,300,000.

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: Gulf Shoreline at Point Au Fer Island at a total cost of $43,400,000.

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: Modification of Caernarvon Diversion at a total cost of $20,700,000.

children.label: (D)
children.own_text: Modification of Davis Pond Diversion at a total cost of $64,200,000.

children.heading: Reports
children.own_text: Not later than December 31, 2009, the Secretary shall submit feasibility reports on the projects described in paragraph (1) to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: Feasibility reports
children.own_text: Not later than December 31, 2008, the Secretary shall submit to Congress feasibility reports on the following projects referred to in the restoration plan:

children.label: (i)
children.own_text: Multipurpose Operation of Houma Navigation Lock at a total cost of $18,100,000.

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: Terrebonne Basin Barrier Shoreline Restoration at a total cost of $124,600,000.

children.label: (iii)
children.own_text: Small Diversion at Convent/Blind River at a total cost of $88,000,000.

children.label: (iv)
children.own_text: Amite River Diversion Canal Modification at a total cost of $5,600,000.

children.label: (v)
children.own_text: Medium Diversion at White's Ditch at a total cost of $86,100,000.

children.label: (vi)
children.own_text: Convey Atchafalaya River Water to Northern Terrebonne Marshes at a total cost of $221,200,000.

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Construction
children.own_text: The Secretary may carry out the projects under subparagraph (A) substantially in accordance with the plans and subject to the conditions, recommended in a final report of the Chief of Engineers if a favorable report of the Chief is completed by not later than December 31, 2010.

children.heading: Construction
children.own_text: No appropriations shall be made to construct any project under this subsection if the report under paragraph (2) or paragraph (3), as the case may be, has not been approved by resolutions adopted by the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: Credit
children.own_text: The Secretary shall credit, in accordance with section 221 of the Flood Control Act 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d-5b), toward the non- Federal share of the cost of a study or project under this title the cost of work carried out in the coastal Louisiana ecosystem by the non- Federal interest for the project before the date of the execution of the partnership agreement for the study or project.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Sources of Funds
children.own_text: The non-Federal interest may use, and the Secretary shall accept, funds provided by a Federal agency under any other Federal program, to satisfy, in whole or in part, the non-Federal share of the cost of the study or project if the Federal agency that provides the funds determines that the funds are authorized to be used to carry out the study or project.

children.label: (c)
children.heading: Nongovernmental Organizations
children.own_text: A nongovernmental organization shall be eligible to contribute all or a portion of the non-Federal share of the cost of a project under this title.

children.label: (d)
children.heading: Treatment of Credit Between Projects
children.own_text: Any credit provided under this section toward the non-Federal share of the cost of a study or project under this title may be applied toward the non-Federal share of the cost of any other study or project under this title.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: To ensure that the contributions of the non-Federal interest equal the non-Federal share of the cost of a study or project under this title during each 5-year period beginning after the date of commencement of the first study or project under this title, the Secretary shall--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: monitor for each study or project under this title the non-Federal provision of cash, in-kind services and materials, and land, easements, rights-of- way, relocations, and disposal areas; and

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: manage the requirement of the non-Federal interest to provide for each such study or project cash, in-kind services and materials, and land, easements, rights-of-way, relocations, and disposal areas.

children.heading: Other monitoring
children.own_text: The Secretary shall conduct monitoring separately for the study phase, construction phase, preconstruction engineering and design phase, and planning phase for each project authorized on or after the date of enactment of this Act for all or any portion of the coastal Louisiana ecosystem.

children.label: (f)
children.heading: Audits
children.own_text: Credit for land, easements, rights-of-way, relocations, and disposal areas (including land value and incidental costs) provided under this section, and the cost of work provided under this section, shall be subject to audit by the Secretary.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: Notwithstanding section 209 of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962-2) or any other provision of law, in carrying out any project or activity under this title or any other provision of law to protect, conserve, and restore the coastal Louisiana ecosystem, the Secretary may determine that--
the project or activity is justified by the environmental benefits derived by the coastal Louisiana ecosystem; and
no further economic justification for the project or activity shall be required if the Secretary determines that the project or activity is cost effective.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Limitation on Applicability
children.own_text: Subsection (a) shall not apply to any separable element of a project intended to produce benefits that are predominantly unrelated to the protection, preservation, and restoration of the coastal Louisiana ecosystem.

sections.label: SEC. 7009.
sections.heading: INDEPENDENT REVIEW
sections.title: VII
sections.own_text: The Secretary shall establish a council, to be known as the ``Louisiana Water Resources Council'', which shall serve as the exclusive peer review panel for activities conducted by the Corps of Engineers in the areas in the State of Louisiana declared as major disaster areas in accordance with section 401 of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 5170) in response to Hurricane Katrina or Rita of 2005, in accordance with the requirements of section 2034.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: The Secretary shall expedite completion of the reports for the following projects and, if the Secretary determines that a project is feasible, proceed directly to project preconstruction engineering and design:
The projects identified in the study of comprehensive hurricane protection authorized by title I of the Energy and Water Development Appropriations Act, 2006 (119 Stat. 2447).

The projects identified in the Southwest Coastal Louisiana hurricane and storm damage reduction study authorized by the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives on December 7, 2005.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Submission of Reports
children.own_text: Upon completion of the reports identified in subsection (a), the Secretary shall submit the reports to the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives.

sections.label: SEC. 7011.
sections.heading: REPORTING
sections.title: VII
sections.own_text: Not later than 6 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate a report, including a description of--

children.own_text: the projects authorized and undertaken under this title;
the construction status of the projects;
the cost to date and the expected final cost of each project undertaken under this title; and
the benefits and environmental impacts of the projects.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: The Secretary is authorized to--

raise levee heights where necessary and otherwise enhance the Lake Pontchartrain and Vicinity project and the West Bank and Vicinity project to provide the level of protection necessary to achieve the certification required for a 100-year level of flood protection in accordance with the national flood insurance program under the base flood elevations current at the time of construction of the levee;
modify the 17th Street, Orleans Avenue, and London Avenue drainage canals in the city of New Orleans and install pumps and closure structures at or near the lakefront at Lake Pontchartrain;
armor critical elements of the New Orleans hurricane and storm damage reduction system;
modify the Inner Harbor Navigation Canal to increase the reliability of the flood protection system for the city of New Orleans;
replace or modify certain non-Federal levees in Plaquemines Parish to incorporate the levees into the New Orleans to Venice Hurricane Protection project;

reinforce or replace flood walls in the existing Lake Pontchartrain and Vicinity project and the existing West Bank and Vicinity project to improve performance of the flood and storm damage reduction systems;
perform one time stormproofing of interior pump stations to ensure the operability of the stations during hurricanes, storms, and high water events;
repair, replace, modify and improve non-Federal levees and associated protection measures in Terrebonne Parish; and

reduce the risk of storm damage to the greater New Orleans metropolitan area by restoring the surrounding wetlands through measures to begin to reverse wetland losses in areas affected by navigation, oil and gas, and other channels and through modification of the Caernarvon Freshwater Diversion structure or its operations.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Cost Sharing
children.own_text: Activities authorized by subsection (a) and section 7013 shall be carried out in a manner that is consistent with the cost-sharing requirements specified in the Emergency Supplemental Appropriations Act for Defense, the Global War on Terror, and Hurricane Recovery, 2006 (Public Law 109-234).

children.label: (c)
children.heading: Conditions
children.own_text: The Secretary shall notify the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate if estimates for the expenditure of funds on any single project or activity identified in subsection (a) exceeds the amount specified for that project or activity in the Emergency Supplemental Appropriations Act for Defense, the Global War on Terror, and Hurricane Recovery, 2006. No appropriation in excess of 25 percent above the amount specified for a project or activity in such Act may be made until an increase in the level of expenditure has been approved by resolutions adopted by the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: Effective beginning on the date of submission of the plan required under paragraph (3), the navigation channel portion of the Mississippi River-Gulf Outlet element of the project for navigation, Mississippi River, Baton Rouge to the Gulf of Mexico, authorized by the Act entitled ``An Act to authorize construction of the Mississippi River-Gulf outlet'', approved March 29, 1956 (70 Stat. 65) and modified by section 844 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1986 (100 Stat. 4177) and section 326 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1996 (110 Stat. 3717), which extends from the Gulf of Mexico to Mile 60 at the southern bank of the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway, is not authorized.

children.heading: Scope
children.own_text: Nothing in this paragraph modifies or deauthorizes the Inner Harbor navigation canal replacement project authorized by that Act of March 29, 1956.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: In general
children.own_text: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives a final report on the deauthorization of the Mississippi River-Gulf outlet, as described under the heading ``Investigations'' under chapter 3 of title II of the Emergency Supplemental Appropriations Act for Defense, the Global War on Terror, and Hurricane Recovery, 2006 (120 Stat. 453).

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Inclusions
children.own_text: At a minimum, the report under subparagraph (A) shall include--

children.label: (i)
children.own_text: a plan to physically modify the Mississippi River-Gulf Outlet and restore the areas affected by the navigation channel;

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: a plan to restore natural features of the ecosystem that will reduce or prevent damage from storm surge;

children.label: (iii)
children.own_text: a plan to prevent the intrusion of saltwater into the waterway;

children.label: (iv)
children.own_text: efforts to integrate the recommendations of the report with the program authorized under section 7003 and the analysis and design authorized by title I of the Energy and Water Development Appropriations Act, 2006 (119 Stat. 2247); and

children.label: (v)
children.own_text: consideration of--

children.label: (I)
children.own_text: use of native vegetation; and

children.label: (II)
children.own_text: diversions of fresh water to restore the Lake Borgne ecosystem.

children.heading: Construction
children.own_text: The Secretary shall carry out a plan to close the Mississippi River-Gulf Outlet and restore and protect the ecosystem substantially in accordance with the plan required under paragraph (3), if the Secretary determines that the project is cost-effective, environmentally acceptable, and technically feasible.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: Reports
children.own_text: With respect to the projects identified in the analysis and design of comprehensive hurricane protection authorized by title I of the Energy and Water Development Appropriations Act, 2006 (119 Stat. 2247), the Secretary shall submit, to the maximum extent practicable, specific project recommendations in a report developed under that title.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: If the President determines that a project recommended in the analysis and design of comprehensive hurricane protection under title I of the Energy and Water Development Appropriations Act, 2006 could--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: address an imminent threat to life and property;

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: prevent a dangerous storm surge from reaching a populated area;

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: prevent the loss of coastal areas that reduce the impact of storm surge;

children.label: (D)
children.own_text: benefit national energy security;

children.label: (E)
children.own_text: protect emergency hurricane evacuation routes or shelters; or

children.label: (F)
children.own_text: address inconsistencies in hurricane protection standards,

children.trailing_text: the President may submit to the President pro tempore of the Senate for authorization a legislative proposal relating to the project, as the President determines to be appropriate.

children.heading: Prioritization
children.own_text: In submitting legislative proposals under paragraph (1), the President shall give priority to any project that, as determined by the President, would--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: to the maximum extent practicable, reduce the risk--

children.label: (i)
children.own_text: of loss of human life;

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: to public safety; and

children.label: (iii)
children.own_text: of damage to property; and

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: minimize costs and environmental impacts.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: In general
children.own_text: Beginning after December 31, 2008, any legislative proposal submitted by the President under paragraph (1) shall be eligible for expedited consideration in accordance with this paragraph.

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Introduction
children.own_text: As soon as practicable after the date of receipt of a legislative proposal under paragraph (1), the Chairman of the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate shall introduce the proposal as a bill, by request, in the Senate.

children.label: (C)
children.heading: Referral
children.own_text: A bill introduced under subparagraph (B) shall be referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate.

children.label: (i)
children.heading: In general
children.own_text: Not later than 45 legislative days after a bill under subparagraph (B) is referred to the committee in accordance with subparagraph (C), the committee shall act on the bill.

children.label: (ii)
children.heading: Failure to act
children.own_text: If the committee fails to act on a bill by the date specified in clause (i), the bill shall be discharged from the committee and placed on the calendar of the Senate.

children.heading: Effective date
children.own_text: The requirements of, and authorities under, this subsection shall expire on December 31, 2010.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: Report
children.own_text: Not later than 120 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives a report describing any modification required to the project for flood damage reduction, Larose to Golden Meadow, Louisiana, to provide the level of protection necessary to achieve the certification required for a 100-year level of flood protection in accordance with the national flood insurance program.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Modifications
children.own_text: The Secretary is authorized to carry out a modification described in subsection (a) if--
the Secretary determines that the modification in the report under subsection (a) is feasible; and
the total cost of the modification does not exceed $90,000,000.

children.label: (c)
children.heading: Requirement
children.own_text: No appropriation shall be made to construct any modification under this section if the report under subsection (a) has not been approved by resolutions adopted by the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: The Secretary may carry out a project for flood damage reduction in Lower Jefferson Parish, Louisiana.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Existing Studies
children.own_text: In carrying out the project, the Secretary shall use, to the maximum extent practicable, existing studies for projects for flood damage reduction in the vicinity of Lower Jefferson Parish, Louisiana, prepared under section 205 of the Flood Control Act of 1948 (33 U.S.C. 701s).

children.label: (c)
children.heading: Construction
children.own_text: The Secretary may proceed to construction or complete the construction of projects in Lower Jefferson Parish if the projects are being developed or carried out under section 205 of the Flood Control Act of 1948 as of the date of enactment of this Act.

children.label: (d)
children.heading: Authorization of Appropriations
children.own_text: There is authorized to be appropriated $100,000,000 to carry out this section.

sections.label: SEC. 8001.
sections.heading: DEFINITIONS
sections.title: VIII
sections.title_heading: UPPER MISSISSIPPI RIVER AND ILLINOIS WATER-WAY SYSTEM
sections.own_text: In this title, the following definitions apply:

children.heading: Plan
children.own_text: The term ``Plan'' means the project for navigation and ecosystem improvements for the Upper Mississippi River and Illinois Waterway System: Report of the Chief of Engineers, dated December 15, 2004.

children.heading: Upper mississippi river and illinois waterway system
children.own_text: The term ``Upper Mississippi River and Illinois Waterway System'' means the projects for navigation and ecosystem restoration authorized by Congress for--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: the segment of the Mississippi River from the confluence with the Ohio River, River Mile 0.0, to Upper St. Anthony Falls Lock in Minneapolis-St. Paul, Minnesota, River Mile 854.0; and

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: the Illinois Waterway from its confluence with the Mississippi River at Grafton, Illinois, River Mile 0.0, to T.J. O'Brien Lock in Chicago, Illinois, River Mile 327.0.

sections.label: SEC. 8002.
sections.heading: NAVIGATION IMPROVEMENTS AND RESTORATION
sections.title: VIII
sections.title_heading: UPPER MISSISSIPPI RIVER AND ILLINOIS WATER-WAY SYSTEM
sections.own_text: Except as modified by this title, the Secretary shall undertake navigation improvements and restoration of the ecosystem for the Upper Mississippi River and Illinois Waterway System substantially in accordance with the Plan and subject to the conditions described therein.

sections.label: SEC. 8003.
sections.heading: AUTHORIZATION OF CONSTRUCTION OF NAVIGATION IMPROVEMENTS
sections.title: VIII
sections.title_heading: UPPER MISSISSIPPI RIVER AND ILLINOIS WATER-WAY SYSTEM

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The Secretary shall--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: construct mooring facilities at Locks 12, 14, 18, 20, 22, 24, and LaGrange Lock or other alternative locations that are economically and environmentally feasible;

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: provide switchboats at Locks 20 through 25; and

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: conduct development and testing of an appointment scheduling system.

children.heading: Authorization of appropriations
children.own_text: The total cost of projects authorized under this subsection shall be $256,000,000. Such costs are to be paid half from amounts appropriated from the general fund of the Treasury and half from amounts appropriated from the Inland Waterways Trust Fund. Such sums shall remain available until expended.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The Secretary shall construct new 1,200- foot locks at Locks 20, 21, 22, 24, and 25 on the Upper Mississippi River and at LaGrange Lock and Peoria Lock on the Illinois Waterway.

children.heading: Authorization of appropriations
children.own_text: The total cost of projects authorized under this subsection shall be $1,948,000,000. Such costs are to be paid half from amounts appropriated from the general fund of the Treasury and half from amounts appropriated from the Inland Waterways Trust Fund. Such sums shall remain available until expended.

children.label: (c)
children.heading: Concurrence
children.own_text: The mitigation required for the projects authorized under subsections (a) and (b), including any acquisition of lands or interests in lands, shall be undertaken or acquired concurrently with lands and interests in lands for the projects authorized under subsections (a) and (b), and physical construction required for the purposes of mitigation shall be undertaken concurrently with the physical construction of such projects.

sections.label: SEC. 8004.
sections.heading: ECOSYSTEM RESTORATION AUTHORIZATION
sections.title: VIII
sections.title_heading: UPPER MISSISSIPPI RIVER AND ILLINOIS WATER-WAY SYSTEM

children.label: (a)
children.heading: Operation
children.own_text: To ensure the environmental sustainability of the existing Upper Mississippi River and Illinois Waterway System, the Secretary shall modify, consistent with requirements to avoid adverse effects on navigation, the operation of the Upper Mississippi River and Illinois Waterway System to address the cumulative environmental impacts of operation of the system and improve the ecological integrity of the Upper Mississippi River and Illinois River.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The Secretary shall carry out, consistent with requirements to avoid adverse effects on navigation, ecosystem restoration projects to attain and maintain the sustainability of the ecosystem of the Upper Mississippi River and Illinois River in accordance with the general framework outlined in the Plan.

children.heading: Projects included
children.own_text: Ecosystem restoration projects may include--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: island building;

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: construction of fish passages;

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: floodplain restoration;

children.label: (D)
children.own_text: water level management (including water drawdown);

children.label: (E)
children.own_text: backwater restoration;

children.label: (F)
children.own_text: side channel restoration;

children.label: (G)
children.own_text: wing dam and dike restoration and modification;

children.label: (H)
children.own_text: island and shoreline protection;

children.label: (I)
children.own_text: topographical diversity;

children.label: (J)
children.own_text: dam point control;

children.label: (K)
children.own_text: use of dredged material for environmental purposes;

children.label: (L)
children.own_text: tributary confluence restoration;

children.label: (M)
children.own_text: spillway, dam, and levee modification to benefit the environment; and

children.label: (N)
children.own_text: land and easement acquisition.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: In general
children.own_text: Except as provided in subparagraphs (B) and (C), the Federal share of the cost of carrying out an ecosystem restoration project under this subsection shall be 65 percent.

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Exception for certain restoration projects
children.own_text: In the case of a project under this section for ecosystem restoration, the Federal share of the cost of carrying out the project shall be 100 percent if the project--

children.label: (i)
children.own_text: is located below the ordinary high water mark or in a connected backwater;

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: modifies the operation of structures for navigation; or

children.label: (iii)
children.own_text: is located on federally owned land.

children.label: (C)
children.heading: Savings clause
children.own_text: Nothing in this subsection affects the applicability of section 906(e) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1986 (33 U.S.C. 2283(e)).

children.label: (D)
children.heading: Nongovernmental organizations
children.own_text: In accordance with section 221 of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d-5b), for any project carried out under this title, a non-Federal sponsor may include a nonprofit entity, with the consent of the affected local government.

children.heading: Land acquisition
children.own_text: The Secretary may acquire land or an interest in land for an ecosystem restoration project from a willing seller through conveyance of--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: fee title to the land; or

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: a flood plain conservation easement.

children.label: (c)
children.heading: Monitoring
children.own_text: The Secretary shall carry out a long term resource monitoring, computerized data inventory and analysis, and applied research program for the Upper Mississippi River and Illinois River to determine trends in ecosystem health, to understand systemic changes, and to help identify restoration needs. The program shall consider and adopt the monitoring program established under section 1103(e)(1)(A)(ii) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1986 (33 U.S.C. 652(e)(1)(A)(ii)).

children.label: (d)
children.heading: Ecosystem Restoration Preconstruction Engineering and Design
Restoration design
children.own_text: Before initiating the construction of any individual ecosystem restoration project, the Secretary shall--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: establish ecosystem restoration goals and identify specific performance measures designed to demonstrate ecosystem restoration;

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: establish the without-project condition or baseline for each performance indicator; and

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: for each separable element of the ecosystem restoration, identify specific target goals for each performance indicator.

children.heading: Outcomes
children.own_text: Performance measures identified under paragraph (1)(A) shall include specific measurable environmental outcomes, such as changes in water quality, hydrology, or the well-being of indicator species the population and distribution of which are representative of the abundance and diversity of ecosystem-dependent aquatic and terrestrial species.

children.heading: Restoration design
children.own_text: Restoration design carried out as part of ecosystem restoration shall include a monitoring plan for the performance measures identified under paragraph (1)(A), including--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: a timeline to achieve the identified target goals; and

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: a timeline for the demonstration of project completion.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: In carrying out the environmental sustainability, ecosystem restoration, and monitoring activities authorized in this section, the Secretary shall consult with the Secretary of the Interior and the States of Illinois, Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri, and Wisconsin.

children.heading: Funding agreements
children.own_text: The Secretary is authorized to enter into agreements with the Secretary of the Interior, the Upper Mississippi River Basin Association, and natural resource and conservation agencies of the States of Illinois, Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri, and Wisconsin to provide for the direct participation of and transfer of funds to such entities for the planning, implementation, and evaluation of projects and programs established by this section.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this subsection $1,717,000,000, of which not more than $245,000,000 shall be available for projects described in subsection (b)(2)(B) and not more than $48,000,000 shall be available for projects described in subsection (b)(2)(J). Such sums shall remain available until expended.

children.heading: Limitation on available funds
children.own_text: Of the amounts made available under paragraph (1), not more than $35,000,000 in any fiscal year may be used for land acquisition under subsection (b)(4).

children.heading: Individual project limit
children.own_text: Other than for projects described in subparagraphs (B) and (J) of subsection (b)(2), the total cost of any single project carried out under this subsection shall not exceed $25,000,000.

children.heading: Monitoring
children.own_text: In addition to amounts authorized under paragraph (1), there are authorized $10,420,000 per fiscal year to carry out the monitoring program under subsection (c) if such sums are not appropriated pursuant to section 1103(e)(4) the Water Resources Development Act of 1986 (33 U.S.C. 652(e)(4)).

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: Not later than June 30, 2009, and every 4 years thereafter, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives an implementation report that--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: includes baselines, milestones, goals, and priorities for ecosystem restoration projects; and

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: measures the progress in meeting the goals.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The Secretary shall appoint and convene an advisory panel to provide independent guidance in the development of each implementation report under paragraph (1).

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Panel members
children.own_text: Panel members shall include--

children.label: (i)
children.own_text: one representative of each of the State resource agencies (or a designee of the Governor of the State) from each of the States of Illinois, Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri, and Wisconsin;

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: one representative of the Department of Agriculture;

children.label: (iii)
children.own_text: one representative of the Department of Transportation;

children.label: (iv)
children.own_text: one representative of the United States Geological Survey;

children.label: (v)
children.own_text: one representative of the United States Fish and Wildlife Service;

children.label: (vi)
children.own_text: one representative of the Environmental Protection Agency;

children.label: (vii)
children.own_text: one representative of affected landowners;

children.label: (viii)
children.own_text: two representatives of conservation and environmental advocacy groups; and

children.label: (ix)
children.own_text: two representatives of agriculture and industry advocacy groups.

children.label: (C)
children.heading: Chairperson
children.own_text: The Secretary shall serve as chairperson of the advisory panel.

children.label: (D)
children.heading: Application of federal advisory committee act
children.own_text: The Advisory Panel and any working group established by the Advisory Panel shall not be considered an advisory committee under the Federal Advisory Committee Act (5 U.S.C. App.).

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The Secretary, in consultation with the Advisory Panel, shall develop a system to rank proposed projects.

children.heading: Priority
children.own_text: The ranking system shall give greater weight to projects that restore natural river processes, including those projects listed in subsection (b)(2).

sections.label: SEC. 8005.
sections.heading: COMPARABLE PROGRESS
sections.title: VIII
sections.title_heading: UPPER MISSISSIPPI RIVER AND ILLINOIS WATER-WAY SYSTEM

children.label: (a)
children.heading: In General
children.own_text: As the Secretary conducts pre-engineering, design, and construction for projects authorized under this title, the Secretary shall--
select appropriate milestones;
determine, at the time of such selection, whether the projects are being carried out at comparable rates; and
make an annual report to Congress, beginning in fiscal year 2009, regarding whether the projects are being carried out at a comparable rate.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: No Comparable Rate
children.own_text: If the Secretary or Congress determines under subsection (a)(2) that projects authorized under this title are not moving toward completion at a comparable rate, annual funding requests for the projects shall be adjusted to ensure that the projects move toward completion at a comparable rate in the future.

sections.label: SEC. 9001.
sections.heading: SHORT TITLE
sections.title: IX
sections.own_text: This title may be cited as the ``National Levee Safety Act of 2007''.

sections.label: SEC. 9002.
sections.heading: DEFINITIONS
sections.title: IX
sections.own_text: In this title, the following definitions apply:

children.heading: Committee
children.own_text: The term ``committee'' means the Committee on Levee Safety established by section 9003(a).

children.heading: Inspection
children.own_text: The term ``inspection'' means an actual inspection of a levee--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: to establish the global information system location of the levee;

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: to determine the general condition of the levee; and

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: to estimate the number of structures and population at risk and protected by the levee that would be adversely impacted if the levee fails or water levels exceed the height of the levee.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: In general
children.own_text: The term ``levee'' means an embankment, including floodwalls--

children.label: (i)
children.own_text: the primary purpose of which is to provide hurricane, storm, and flood protection relating to seasonal high water, storm surges, precipitation, and other weather events; and

children.label: (ii)
children.own_text: that normally is subject to water loading for only a few days or weeks during a year.

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Inclusion
children.own_text: The term includes structures along canals that constrain water flows and are subject to more frequent water loadings but that do not constitute a barrier across a watercourse.

children.heading: State
children.own_text: The term ``State'' means--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: a State;

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: the District of Columbia;

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico; and

children.label: (D)
children.own_text: any other territory or possession of the United States.

children.heading: State levee safety agency
children.own_text: The term ``State levee safety agency'' means the agency of a State that has regulatory authority over the safety of any non-Federal levee in the State.

children.heading: United states
children.own_text: The term ``United States'', when used in a geographical sense, means all of the States.

children.label: (a)
children.heading: Establishment
children.own_text: There is established a committee to be known as the ``Committee on Levee Safety''.

children.label: (b)
children.heading: Membership
children.own_text: The committee shall be composed of 16 members as follows:
The Secretary (or the Secretary's designee), who shall serve as the chairperson of the Committee.
The Administrator of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (or the Administrator's designee).
The following 14 members appointed by the Secretary:

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: Eight representatives of State levee safety agencies, one from each of the eight civil works divisions of the Corps of Engineers.

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: Two representatives of the private sector who have expertise in levee safety.

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: Two representatives of local and regional governmental agencies who have expertise in levee safety.

children.label: (D)
children.own_text: Two representatives of Indian tribes who have expertise in levee safety.

children.heading: Development of recommendations for national levee safety program
children.own_text: The committee shall develop recomendations for a national levee safety program, including a strategic plan for implementation of the program.

children.heading: Report
children.own_text: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the committee shall submit to the Secretary, the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives, and the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate a report containing the recommendations developed under paragraph (1).

children.label: (d)
children.heading: Purposes
children.own_text: In developing recommendations under subsection (c)(1), the committee shall ensure that the national levee safety program meets the following goals:

Ensuring the protection of human life and property by levees through the development of technologically, economically, socially, and environmentally feasible programs and procedures for hazard reduction and mitigation relating to levees.
Encouraging use of the best available engineering policies and procedures for levee site investigation, design, construction, operation and maintenance, and emergency preparedness.

Encouraging the establishment and implementation of an effective national levee safety program that may be delegated to qualified States for implementation, including identification of incentives and disincentives for State levee safety programs.
Ensuring that levees are operated and maintained in accordance with appropriate and protective standards by conducting an inventory and inspection of levees.
Developing and supporting public education and awareness projects to increase public acceptance and support of State and national levee safety programs.
Building public awareness of the residual risks associated with living in levee protected areas.
Developing technical assistance materials for State and national levee safety programs.
Developing methods to provide technical assistance relating to levee safety to non-Federal entities.
Developing technical assistance materials, seminars, and guidelines relating to the physical integrity of levees in the United States.

children.label: (e)
children.heading: Compensation of Members
children.own_text: A member of the committee shall serve without compensation.

children.label: (f)
children.heading: Travel Expenses
children.own_text: To the extent amounts are made available in advance in appropriations Acts, the Secretary shall reimburse a member of the committee for travel expenses, including per diem in lieu of subsistence, at rates authorized for an employee of a Federal agency under subchapter I of chapter 57 of title 5, United States Code, while away from the home or regular place of business of the member in performance of services for the committee.

children.label: (g)
children.heading: Applicability of Federal Advisory Committee Act
children.own_text: The Federal Advisory Committee Act (5 U.S.C. App.) shall not apply to the committee.

children.heading: In general
children.own_text: Not later than one year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall establish and maintain a database with an inventory of the Nation's levees.

children.heading: Contents
children.own_text: The database shall include--

children.label: (A)
children.own_text: location information of all Federal levees in the Nation (including global information system information) and, for non-Federal levees, such information on levee location as is provided to the Secretary by State and local governmental agencies;

children.label: (B)
children.own_text: utilizing such information as is available, the general condition of each levee; and

children.label: (C)
children.own_text: an estimate of the number of structures and population at risk and protected by each levee that would be adversely impacted if the levee fails or water levels exceed the height of the levee.

children.label: (A)
children.heading: Availability to federal, state, and local governmental agencies
children.own_text: The Secretary shall make all of the information in the database available to appropriate Federal, State, and local governmental agencies.

children.label: (B)
children.heading: Availability to the public
children.own_text: The Secretary shall make the information in the database described in paragraph (2)(A), and such other information in the database as the Secretary determines appropriate, available to the public.

children.heading: Federal levees
children.own_text: The Secretary, at Federal expense, shall establish an inventory and conduct an inspection of all federally owned and operated levees.

children.heading: Federally constructed, nonfederally operated and maintained levees
children.own_text: The Secretary shall establish an inventory and conduct an inspection of all federally constructed, non- federally operated and maintained levees, at the original cost share for the project.

children.heading: Participating levees
children.own_text: For non-Federal levees the owners of which are participating in the emergency response to natural disasters program established under section 5 of the Act entitled ``An Act authorizing the construction of certain public works on rivers and harbors for flood control, and for other purposes'', approved August 18, 1941 (33 U.S.C. 701n), the Secretary shall establish an inventory and conduct an inspection of each such levee if the owner of the levee requests such inspection. The Federal share of the cost of an inspection under this paragraph shall be 65 percent.

sections.label: SEC. 9005.
sections.heading: LIMITATIONS ON STATUTORY CONSTRUCTION
sections.title: IX
sections.own_text: Nothing in this title shall be construed as--

children.own_text: creating any liability of the United States or its officers or employees for the recovery of damages caused by an action or failure to act; or
relieving an owner or operator of a levee of a legal duty, obligation, or liability incident to the ownership or operation of a levee.

sections.label: SEC. 9006.
sections.heading: AUTHORIZATION OF APPROPRIATIONS
sections.title: IX
sections.own_text: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this title $20,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2008 through 2013.
